exposure: prenatal Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression (CES-D) scores
cohort: The study participants were 225 individuals from the MADRES (Maternal and Developmental Risks From Environmental and Social Stressors) cohort.
finding: Higher prenatal perceived stress and depressive symptoms were associated with greater 1-year postpartum blood pressure, whereas higher neighborhood social cohesion was associated with lower 1-year postpartum blood pressure in certain subgroups.
